summary: Akio Donohashi works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1968 to 1977 and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Minoura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Otani University (attested 1995, 2007–2013), Uiduk University (attested 1996), Stanford University (2012–2013), and Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Akio Tanabe specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1988, PhD 2006) and held positions at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (professor 2015).

Akira Fujieda specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), where he served from 1937 and became professor in 1968, alongside appointments at Northwest Institute, Copenhagen, and UC Berkeley.
Akira Hataya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1962–1975) and taught at Waseda, Rissho, and ICPBS.

Akira Miyaji specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and DLitt at Nagoya University, where he taught (~1977–2007), and later served at Hirosaki University, Shizuoka Prefectural Museum, and Ryukoku University.
Akira Momiyama is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1972 to 1980 and served as a professor at Saitama University from circa 1993 to 2018.

Akira Mukai works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Hokkaido University, where he served as an assistant (attested 1978), and later became a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kyoshi Takahama and at Heidelberg University, holding posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, and Ryukoku University.

Akira Sadakata is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris. He served as professor and emeritus professor at Tokai University.

Akira Saito specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and earned his PhD at the Australian National University, holding professorships at the University of Tokyo, ICPBS, and IIBS.

Akira Shimada specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at College of Art, Delhi under Rajeev Lochan and at SOAS under Daud Ali, later holding posts at the British Museum and SUNY New Paltz.

Akira Suganuma was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University, where he held assistant (attested 1962) and associate professor (1991–1994) posts, and lectured at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Akira Takeda was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held teaching posts at Tokyo Woman's Christian University, served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1965–1991), and became professor emeritus at Meikai University.
Akira Yamada was a philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1944 to 1947 under Tokuryu Yamauchi and held a post at Nanzan University from circa 1957 to 1967.

Akira Yuyama was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics scholar who studied at ANU under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, Leiden, and Tokyo University of the Arts. He held posts at ANU, IIBS, IRIAB, and Soka University.

Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as professor and professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 1982, 2014) and as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Akong Tulku Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre in 1967 and served as its abbot (attested 2009).
Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She is a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago and a researcher at Ghent University (both attested 2026).
